title: Payroll Assistant
description:
A health services organisation operating across multiple sites in the South East has a new opportunity for a part-time Payroll Assistant in their Maidstone office.

The Payroll Assistant will provide day-to-day support to the Payroll Manager, helping to collate payroll information and respond to payroll queries. This is a key support role ensuring employees are paid accurately and on time, and that payroll records are maintained to a high standard of accuracy and confidentiality.

The role is based in their Maidstone office will initially be on a temporary basis (4-month contract), with a view to becoming permanent.

Responsibilitiesof the Management Accountant Role:
- Collate and check payroll data each pay period, including new starters, leavers, changes to pay, overtime, and absence records
- Support the Payroll Manager in the preparation and processing of the monthly/weekly payroll run
- Act as a first point of contact for payroll queries from employees and managers, escalating more complex issues to the Payroll Manager
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date payroll and personnel records in line with data protection requirements
- Assist with the calculation and processing of statutory payments (e.g. SSP, SMP, SPP) and deductions (e.g. tax, National Insurance, pension contributions)
- Help reconcile payroll data against timesheets, HR systems, and other source records
- Support month-end and year-end payroll processes, including P60s, P11 Ds, and other statutory reporting
- Liaise with HR and Finance teams to ensure payroll information is accurate and consistent across systems
- Assist with filing, record-keeping, and general administrative tasks within the payroll function
- Support the Payroll Manager with ad hoc payroll projects and process improvements as required.

Requirementsof the Management Accountant role:
- Previous experience in a payroll, HR, or finance administration role is essential
- Good numeracy skills and a high level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
- Confident communicator, comfortable handling queries from employees at all levels
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and confident using payroll or HR software systems
- Trustworthy and discreet when handling sensitive and confidential information
- A proactive, can-do attitude and willingness to learn.

Benefits of the Management Accountant role:
- 22 days holiday plus Bank Holidays
- On-site parking
- Office-based - Monday to Friday, 9 to 2:30
- £32,000 to £36,000 (pro rata) (£16 to £18 p/h), dependent on experience.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: This is a key role within our multidisciplinary team, supporting clinicians by ensuring incoming clinical correspondence is reviewed, processed and accurately recorded. You will identify relevant clinical information, update patient records and ensure correspondence is directed to the right person or team. The role will suit someone who enjoys working with detailed information, follows processes carefully and can use their judgement to identify what can be safely managed and what needs clinical input. You will help reduce unnecessary GP workload while recognising when something is outside your remit and needs to be escalated. Day-to-day work may include reviewing hospital letters, investigation results and other clinical correspondence, extracting and coding relevant information, updating patient records, filing documentation and directing tasks to the appropriate team. You may also support note summarising and other activities that maintain clear, accurate clinical records. Accuracy and patient safety are at the heart of this role. You will need to manage your workload, follow practice and national guidance, and know when to seek advice from a GP, supervisor or manager. By ensuring clinical information is handled accurately, promptly and safely, you will help our clinicians work effectively and support patient care. As a Clinical Administrator, you will help keep the practices clinical and administrative processes running smoothly. Your main duties will include processing incoming clinical correspondence, accurately updating patient records, reviewing and coding clinical information, and ensuring information is directed to the appropriate team member. You will support the processing of hospital and clinic letters, results, safeguarding information and electronic data, as well as summarising new patient records, supporting registrations and managing out-of-area correspondence. You will also monitor recalls, screening results and high-risk medication monitoring to help ensure important follow-up is not missed. The role includes supporting QOF, audits, enhanced services and other quality improvement work, alongside patient recall programmes such as immunisations and cervical screening. You will also process insurance and medical reports, monitor the practice email account and provide wider administrative support when required. Working closely with the clinical team, you will identify and escalate complex or sensitive issues appropriately and support effective communication across the practice. You will also contribute to team meetings and training and help new colleagues learn practice processes. High standards of confidentiality, information governance and accuracy are essential. Job Description Clinical Administrator Job Title: Clinical Administrator Responsible to: Administration Lead, Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Partnership Hours: TBA Job Summary The Clinical Administrator provides vital support to the multidisciplinary team by managing and processing clinical correspondence and patient records in line with practice and national guidelines. The role focuses on streamlining workflows to reduce unnecessary GP administration, ensuring accurate coding and filing of information, and directing more complex items to the appropriate clinician for review. The post-holder will work as part of the Clinical Administration team, prioritising their workload effectively, maintaining strict confidentiality at all times, and knowing when to escalate matters to supervisors or clinicians. Roles and Responsibilities Ensure all incoming and internal correspondence is stored in patient records. Review and Read Code clinical correspondence before forwarding to clinicians. Process and file hospital letters, reports, emails and other correspondence. Code diagnoses, procedures and investigations accurately. Refer complex or high-risk documents, including safeguarding issues, to the relevant clinician. Summarise new patient records (manual and GP2GP) and process registrations, transfers, and out-of-area notifications. Manage incoming test results, redirect unmatched pathology, and process screening and monitoring results (e.g. diabetic eye screening, mammograms, DMARD recalls). Process Out of Hours reports and other external communications. Maintain accurate documentation for insurance reports, medical reports and private letters. Monitor the practice email inbox, flagging urgent queries promptly. Support enhanced service administration, QOF monitoring, recalls (e.g. immunisations, smears, chronic disease), and audits. Run EMIS searches as required. Provide administrative cover for other team members when necessary. Open, scan, distribute and file post; manage photocopying and record requests. Assist with training and mentoring of new staff. Maintain a tidy office environment and adhere to a clear desk policy. Teamwork & Communication Work as part of the Clinical Administration Team and the wider practice team. Build effective working relationships with colleagues, patients and external organisations. Communicate clearly and professionally, ensuring confidentiality at all times. Participate in meetings and training, including occasional sessions outside normal hours. General Responsibilities Confidentiality Patients entrust the practice with sensitive information and staff must respect this confidentiality at all times. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues or the practice may only be shared in line with GDPR and practice policies. Health & Safety Follow practice health and safety policies, including infection prevention and control. Use personal security systems as required. Identify risks, manage work safely, and report concerns promptly. Maintain work areas in a safe, hazard-free condition. Equality & Diversity Promote equality of opportunity and respect the rights of patients, carers and colleagues. Act in ways that recognise diversity and ensure fairness, consistent with policy and legislation. Respect privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs at all times. Personal & Professional Development Participate in annual appraisal and performance reviews. Take responsibility for ongoing learning and development.
